venture.description: A belt buckle that folds down to hold a beverage, freeing the user's hands.
venture.note: He holds up the buckle and demonstrates it.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Pitches Bev Buckle, a belt buckle that holds a beverage, seeking $50k for 10% equity.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks how the founder came up with the idea for the product.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he was in college and wanted to free his hands to show off his dance moves.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks to see one of the buckles and handle it.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks if the product comes with the belt included.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Hands the product over and clarifies that it does not come with the belt.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if a magnet is used to hold the buckle closed.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms that a magnet holds it closed.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if the founder has any sales currently.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States he has traveled across America and sold over four thousand units.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks over what period of time those sales were made.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Clarifies the sales were made over a period of four years.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks what the unit sales translate to in dollar revenue.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States that revenue is at three hundred and forty thousand dollars.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if the product has a patent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms that he has a patent.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks what the cost is to manufacture the buckles.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains it costs ten dollars to make and sells for thirty-five to one hundred and ten.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks Daymond if the manufacturing cost is a good price.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Agrees that it is a pretty good price.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks the founder what his full-time job is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he just finished school to be an unexploded ordnance technician.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks what an unexploded ordnance technician means.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains it involves identifying and remediating unexploded military ordnance.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Compares the job to the movie The Hurt Locker, looking for bombs.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms the comparison to The Hurt Locker is accurate.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Asks if the founder actually wants to do that dangerous job.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains it is plan B to provide for his family and his first child on the way.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Jokes that a mistake on the job means ending up in five pieces.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Jokes back that there are no mistakes in his line of work.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks what the game plan is for the next day if he gets the investment.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Offers the panel a choice between two envelopes outlining his plans.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Expresses liking for the founder and asks the panel which envelope to open.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Votes to open envelope number one.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the first list contains retailers who want the product in all their stores.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Reads out the names of the major retailers on the first list.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains the second list contains major raceways that want the buckle sold trackside.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Reads out the names of the major raceways on the second list.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Asks if any of the companies on the lists have actually written a check.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Admits they haven't because a recent defective order caused a problem with his manufacturer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Reacts with surprise to the high defect rate.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Comments that the manufacturing issue is bad news.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks why he wouldn't have taken a purchase order from the listed companies anyway.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he lacks the working capital to supply the orders without an advance check.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks if the founder plans to work full time on the business.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms he will work full time if he is financially able to.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Asks if needing to be financially able means he requires a salary.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Explains he needs to pay bills and would rather avoid working with bombs.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Asks exactly how much money he would need to make it his full-time job.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Estimates he needs two to three thousand dollars to cover his mortgage and bills.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Clarifies if the requested amount is per month.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Confirms the amount needed is per month.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: States the valuation is too high and he lacks time to teach him, so he is out.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Asks how many units of inventory the founder currently holds.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: States he currently has sixty-two units in inventory.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: States the math doesn't add up and the challenges haven't changed, so he is out.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Offers the requested fifty thousand dollars but asks for a seventy-five percent equity stake.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Encourages the founder, saying he just needs guidance and is on the right track.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Offers fifty thousand dollars for a twelve percent royalty on sales, taking no equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that he would rather take the deal than work with bombs.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Pitches his offer, emphasizing the need to grow the business into new sporting goods avenues.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Offers fifty thousand dollars for a fifty-one percent stake to undercut Robert's offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Adds a condition to her offer that the founder cannot take a salary from the investment.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Criticizes Robert's offer, calling it insane to give up seventy-five percent of the company.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Agrees with Kevin that giving up seventy-five percent of the company is crazy.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Agrees that giving up that much equity is crazy.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Tells the founder not to listen to the other sharks and pushes his own offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Argues against Kevin's royalty offer, saying a growing business shouldn't give up cash flow.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Urges the founder to make a decision and close a deal with one of the investors.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Prompts the founder to decide what he is going to do.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Tells the founder he has to pick one of the choices available to him.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Accepts Barbara's offer, stating she is the best person to go into business with.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Compliments the founder for making a smart decision.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Tells the founder he made a mistake with his decision.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Reaffirms that he feels he made a very good decision.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Reiterates that the founder made a mistake by giving up control of his company.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: Thanks the panel of investors as he prepares to leave.

decisions.note: Valuation is too high and he doesn't have the time to teach him.
Math doesn't add up, same challenges for four years, not working smart.
Founder is standing still and will require a lot of time to guide.
Thinks Robert's offer takes too much equity, prefers a royalty deal to save founder from bomb squad.
Wants to beat Robert's greedy offer.

Thinks Barbara is the best person to go into business with.
